# Tooltip

A short hint on hover or focus.

:label[Left out of Multi-brand]{tone="warning"} Customers use any device, and on touch screens hover hints never show; a popover explains a fee instead. Use instead: [Popover](./popover)

## See it live

::preview{id="tooltip/live"}

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** A brief name or hint for a control that already has an accessible name.
- **Not when:** The only place values or important words live, or touch screens, where hover never happens.

Instead:

- [Popover](./popover.md): Opens on click and works on touch.
- [Hover card](./hover-card.md): A richer preview.

::card-grid{id="anatomy-link/tooltip"}

## How Multi-brand uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">An icon with no label</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Not used: always add a word; a popover explains a fee</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> An icon button with a hover hint</div></div><div class="cap">On touch screens hover hints never show; a word says what will happen.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Escape hides it. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It describes its trigger and also shows on keyboard focus. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add tooltip
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Tooltip reads 9 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Tooltip's tokens to change Tooltip alone.

::token-table{component="tooltip"}
